newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks rise to fourth straight record.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks rise to fourth straight record.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose to a record for the fourth straight session Monday as investors stepped in to hunt for bargains after an earlier bout of profit-taking.
The blue-chip IPC share index rose 15.21 points to 4,259.84.
Dealers said trading was quiet and volume was only 85.5 million shares. In the broader market, gainers narrowly outpaced losers, 45 to 42.
"The market got a second wind, earlier selling was not heavy and dealing was quiet," one floor trader said.
"The market was dull. There was no overall trend, apart from financials, that were strong," another trader said.

Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, was the most heavily traded gainer. Its B shares rose 10 centavos (1 centavo) to 3.80 pesos (48 cents), while the A shares gained 8 centavos (1 cent) to 2.05 pesos (26 cents). The two share classes accounted for 22 percent of all shares traded.

Dealers also drew attention to retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana (Comerci), which climbed 48 centavos (6 cents) to 6.86 pesos (86 cents) at relatively brisk trade to head the gainers' list.
"Comerci had lagged far behind recent market gains," a floor trader said.
Traders said some stocks, notably tortilla and corn flour firm Maseca, did not recover from earlier profit-taking. Maseca shed 6 centavos (less than 1 cent) to end at 8.08 pesos ($1.02).
